claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 homogenized above 1100 °C is a uniform, disordered BCC phase.
Al has higher diffusivity than the other elements in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Cooling from the high-temperature BCC state causes localized Al segregation.
Once a threshold local Al concentration is reached, an ordered secondary phase such as B2 nucleates.
Tracer-diffusion measurements will establish Al mobility as the primary trigger for the transformation.
The controlled comparison uses a rapidly quenched sample as the baseline and samples cooled below 10 °C/min and then aged near 800 °C for 1–100 hours.
Thermal exposure around 800 °C provides sufficient activation for significant Al diffusion.
Rapid quenching prevents notable Al segregation and preserves a metastable disordered BCC structure.
Slow cooling and aging near 800 °C allow Al atoms to segregate locally.
Localized Al enrichment occurs at grain boundaries or within grains and supplies nucleation sites for an ordered phase.
Localized Al segregation lowers the nucleation barrier for an ordered phase in the BCC matrix.
Aging can promote ordered-precipitate formation from a quenched compositionally complex alloy.
Supersaturated BCC compositionally complex alloys can decompose during prolonged annealing in the 600–800 °C range.
Slowly cooled and aged Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 will contain more Al-enriched regions than the rapidly quenched baseline.
The Al-enriched regions will exhibit B2-type ordering detectable through distinct diffraction peaks.
Atom-probe tomography will reveal compositional gradients associated with the ordered regions.
The extent of ordering will increase with aging time near 800 °C.
The rapidly quenched baseline remains single-phase disordered BCC with no significant Al segregation.
The proposed segregation-driven transformation requires aging near 800 °C for at least one hour and should not occur at low temperature or under extremely rapid cooling.
Failure to observe both significant Al segregation and an ordered phase relative to the quenched baseline, or failure to observe enhanced Al mobility, would falsify the hypothesis.
